guideline: Best-Worst Scaling methodology with AMT workers evaluating summaries on multiple criteria
Best-Worst Scaling methodology with AMT workers evaluating summaries on multiple criteria
- Workers were instructed to select the best and worst summary based on criteria including fluency, coherence, non-redundancy, opinion consensus, and overall quality.
Annotators were asked to select the best and worst summary according to several criteria.

Workers were advised to read the reviews and rate sentences using one of the following three options. Full support: all the content is reflected in the reviews; Partial support: only some content is reflected in the reviews; No support: content is not reflected in the reviews.

changes_made.explanation: Consolidated duplicate criteria with consistent capitalization, simplified guideline description, and added content support evaluation as separate human evaluation task

overall_notes: Paper focuses on unsupervised abstractive opinion summarization using a hierarchical VAE model (COPYCAT). Evaluation includes both automatic metrics (ROUGE) and comprehensive human evaluation using Best-Worst Scaling with 5 criteria. No LLM-based evaluation was conducted. Human evaluation was rigorous with detailed guidelines and multiple annotators per item.
